09:00.headline: Junior year, quiet inbox?
09:00.topic: Recruiting Reality Check: junior with limited recruiting interest; compare numbers by level, widen target list, keep reaching out
09:00.caption:
Recruiting Reality Check: your player is a junior, and the inbox is quiet. Is it too late?

For most families, no. But waiting for coaches to find him isn't a plan.

✅ Compare his numbers with typical ranges by level, so you know where he realistically fits right now
✅ Widen the target list to include D2, D3, NAIA and JUCO programs that match those numbers
❌ Don't sit back and wait for the phone to ring
❌ Don't panic, and don't stop reaching out. A short, specific email with updated numbers and video keeps doors open

Quiet now doesn't mean quiet forever. Plenty of players keep developing, and many programs keep recruiting well into a player's junior and senior years.

13:00.headline: What goes in his first email
13:00.topic: How-to: coach intro email checklist (basics, 3-4 verified numbers, short video, why this program; player sends it)
13:00.caption:
Your player is ready to email college coaches. What actually belongs in that first message?

The emails that get read are short, specific and easy to act on. A simple checklist:

⚾ The basics up top: grad year, position, high school and travel team, plus GPA
⚾ 3 to 4 verified numbers: things like exit velo, 60 time, throwing velo or pop time, with where and when they were measured
⚾ A short video link: a couple of minutes of clean, recent footage beats a long highlight reel
⚾ Why this program: one or two sentences showing he's looked at the roster, the level and the academics

Have your player write and send it himself, keep it to a few short paragraphs, and include his upcoming schedule.

Knowing which levels fit his numbers first helps him email the right programs.

13:00.caption_instagram:
What goes in his first coach email? Save this checklist ✅

1. Grad year, position, school (plus GPA)
2. 3 to 4 verified numbers, with where they were measured
3. A short video link: recent, clean, a couple of minutes
4. Why this program fits him, in a sentence or two

Short and specific gets read. And it should come from your player, not from you.
